research_question: How much of the S2C-MOGB-Fair gap is caused by selected-ball filtering omitting registered Known classes?

main_result: 16/45 cells omitted at least one registered Known class; 29 unaffected cells were exact zero-change controls. StackOverflow default rescue recovered 8.40pp Known Recall but added 6.23pp false acceptance and lost 13.87pp AUROC; cal-80 rescue lost 15.66pp OOS F1 and added 18.61pp false acceptance. S2C Trainable K1 still won OOS F1 and F1-All in 45/45 pairs.
decision: Class omission is a real Known-coverage defect but not the main S2C-MOGB gap; keep as component attribution and do not present the fallback as an official MOGB repair or new method.
notes: 45 train-only granular-ball fits plus 180 scoring units; class fallback uses train_known only, cal-80 uses calibration_known only, and test labels are evaluation-only. No encoder training or historical artifact overwrite.

research_question: Which selected granular balls carry MOGB-Fair false accepts and Known false rejects, and do purity or tiny clusters explain the gap to S2C Trainable K1?
hypothesis: If MOGB-Fair underperformance is caused mainly by fragmented tiny balls, low-support balls should dominate both error budgets; otherwise risk should remain concentrated in larger balls and change with the boundary on a shared partition.
main_result: 90/90 method cells and 8930 selected-ball rows were audited. The highest-risk 10 percent of balls carry about 89-98 percent of OOS false accepts, but Q3/Q4 support balls rather than tiny balls carry most error budget; purity is nearly always one. Changing only the boundary recovers Known coverage but still trails Trainable K1.
decision: Keep as component-level post-hoc attribution; do not delete balls using test risk or claim official BERT MOGB failure. Purity and tiny-cluster rules are not safe OOS-risk selectors.
notes: Analysis-only; shared partitions and per-ball counts were verified exactly; no model training, threshold selection, partition change, artifact overwrite or test-label selection.

notes: Analysis-only; 45 paired cells and 443400 prediction rows; exact sample/gold alignment and F1-All replay; no training, threshold selection, split change, raw text, or sample IDs in lightweight outputs.

research_question: Can external-baseline OOS SOTA be reached with limited Known and Accuracy cost?

research_question: Does Trainable MiniLM Gate improve the full pipeline when every downstream component is fixed?
hypothesis: Changing only the Gate representation should improve OOS separation and reduce false acceptance if the Trainable Gate effect is real.
main_result: 54 CUDA cells compare Frozen and Trainable K=1 Gates under identical Router/Expert and boundary contracts; Trainable improves OOS F1 and Accuracy and reduces false acceptance in all nine dataset-KIR pairs.
decision: Use this as the direct ablation for the current contribution; keep historical paper four-variant artifacts separate.
notes: No Router/Expert retraining; no OOS training or test selection; corrected full-test Known F1 used; fulltex.tex unchanged.
